extraction.name: SciQ
extraction.description: SciQ is a dataset of 13,679 multiple choice science exam questions spanning biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics, assembled through a crowdsourcing method leveraging domain-specific textbooks and model-suggested answer distractors. It includes both a multiple choice version and a direct-answer reading comprehension version.
extraction.creator: Johannes Welbl, Nelson F. Liu, Matt Gardner
extraction.citeAs: Welbl, J., Liu, N. F., & Gardner, M. (2017). Crowdsourcing Multiple Choice Science Questions. arXiv preprint arXiv:1707.06209.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected via a two-step crowdsourcing process on Amazon Mechanical Turk. First, crowd workers were shown three filtered textbook paragraphs and chose one (or rejected all) to formulate a science exam question and its correct answer. Second, another worker evaluated the question-answer pair for exam quality and created three distractors, aided by selecting up to two distractors suggested by a trained distractor ranking model and writing at least one distractor themselves.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: A small percentage of the passages were obtained from unreleasable texts, which caused the direct answer version of the dataset to be smaller (10,481 training, 887 validation, and 884 test questions) compared to the multiple choice version.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: A base corpus of 28 science study textbooks covering biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics spanning elementary level to introductory college level, sourced from online learning resources including CK-12 and OpenStax.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rule-based document filter classified sentences from textbook paragraphs and accepted paragraphs with a minimum number of acceptable sentences. Sentences were removed if they were questions or exclamations, lacked a verb phrase, contained modal verbs, imperative phrases, demonstrative pronouns, personal pronouns other than third-person, began with pronouns, contained first names, had fewer than 6 or more than 18 tokens or >2 commas, contained special characters other than punctuation, had >3 capitalized tokens, mentioned graphs/tables/links, began with discourse markers, contained absolute wording, or contained instructional vocabulary.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers created questions of 6–30 words with answers up to 3 words querying general principles based on selected textbook passages. In the second step, workers performed validation by judging whether questions were suitable for a school science exam (marking them as ungrammatical, having false answers, unrelated to science, or requiring overly specific background knowledge). Workers then selected up to two machine-suggested distractors and authored at least one distractor manually to reach a total of three distractors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Validation during the distractor task showed that 92.8% of generated question-answer pairs passed quality control criteria. Additionally, a qualitative evaluation showed human evaluators could only distinguish crowdsourced questions from real exam questions 55% of the time, which was not statistically significant compared to random chance.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: A total of 175 crowd workers participated, all required to have Amazon Mechanical Turk Master's status.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A random forest classifier (scikit-learn implementation with 500 trees) trained on real science exam questions was used to score, rank, and suggest plausible answer distractors to annotators.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of reading comprehension and question answering models for multiple-choice and direct-answer science exams, and augmenting training sets for answering real elementary and middle school science questions.
